newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia building group urges rate cut after CPI.
newsitem.headline: Australia building group urges rate cut after CPI.

text.p: The Real Estate Institute of Australia (REIA) on Wednesday urged the Reserve Bank to ease monetary policy again after figures showed underlying inflation at a record low.

"General uncertainty in the economy, continuing low inflation, and consistent high unemployment rates underpin the REIA's assessment that a cut in interest rates will not reignite inflationary pressures," REIA president Don Brindley said in a statement.
Brindley said REIA believed the bank could justifiably cut official cash rates by another 0.5 percentage points.
Australian underlying inflation rose 0.3 percent in the June quarter for an annual rate of 1.7 percent, the lowest annual underlying inflation rate since the series started in 1991.
The Reserve Bank has eased monetary policy four times in the past year, cutting rates by 0.5 percentage points each time. Offical cash rates currently stand at 5.5 percent.
The first rate cut was in July last year, while the most recent was on May 23.
